source: docs/reports/2026-09-07-esp-emu-c6-spike.md §11.1; the spike planning directory's desk-captures/step1-harness.txt, which is the ANSI-stripped step1-harness.cap
capture: espflash flash --monitor of harness/5/fw.elf — the very ELF the emulator ran — in the FOREGROUND under script(1) through a python SIG_DFL exec shim, stopped by `kill -INT <its own espflash pid>` once `=== DONE ===` appeared. One step at a time, port released between steps, lsof/pgrep empty before every open. `=== DONE ===` after 31 s including the flash. The espflash progress bar at the head of the file is part of the capture and is deliberately not trimmed.
note: This transcript predates the in-band [fw-checks-header] line, so this sidecar is the whole header. It is the silicon half of the parity claim in spike report §11.1: memory byte-equal to esp-emu, time is not. The board's eFuse reports chip revision v0.2; esp-emu's synthetic eFuse says v0.3 for the same board, which is why silicon_rev differs across the pair.

a real clock on real flash with real wait states — the 5 ms slice budget fails here at 11,724 us
